## Broadband Infrastructure
Rural Broadband Connectivity, Now!
Our families and businesses need reliable, fast, affordable internet – that’s why Congressman Jack Bergman is achieving and fighting for more connectivity than ever before.
Whether you need to schedule a telehealth appointment with your primary care provider, attend an online class, join a zoom conference, shop online for a big birthday, or start an online career - broadband access is more important than ever, especially in rural and remote communities which have been sidelined for too long.
As a member of the Bipartisan House Rural Broadband Caucus and having started a Rural Connectivity Advisory Committee in Michigan’s First Congressional District, Jack Bergman has been supporting key programs to bring high speed broadband to your Michigan home and business as well as to improve telehealth access across our Nation.
Congressman Bergman has voted to provide billions of dollars for broadband infrastructure reserved for rural and remote areas in Michigan’s First Congressional District.
For Fiscal Year 2021 alone, Congressman Bergman got more than
$2 billion in broadband funds signed into law through programs such as the NTIA Broadband Infrastructure Deployment Grant Program and Tribal Broadband Connectivity Program. Congressman Bergman is advocating for local applicants seeking funds through these programs. He has helped achieve key local investments through these programs such as through the Distance Learning and Telemedicine Grants ( $2.5 million + for MI-1) and the USDA ReConnect Broadband Grant/Loan Program ( $3.5 million + for MI-1), a program that he voted to establish.
In 2020, with COVID-19 suddenly increasing the necessity of broadband, Rep. Bergman voted for nearly
$3.5 billion in emergency broadband funding for telehealth, mapping, and keeping families connected.
Congressman Bergman has also been closely involved in more largescale broadband infrastructure programs operated by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), including the new Rural Digital Opportunity Fund (RDOF). The Rural Digital Opportunity Fund Phase I Auction results in 2021 yielded more than
$200 million to build new broadband infrastructure to over 84,000 locations in MI-1. Jack Bergman, working with local providers receiving funding, has pressured the FCC to ensure these funds are implemented swiftly and efficiently.
Congressman Bergman is leading legislative proposals to bridge the digital divide.
He has introduced bills such as:
H.R.4905 - the Big Tech Accountability for Broadband Act,
which would force Big Tech companies to pay into key rural broadband programs that they benefit from. The programs targeted in this bill are currently by fees on your phone bill, a hidden tax on seniors and working families!
H.R.1610 - the Rural Broadband Window of Opportunity Act is another bill introduced by Jack Bergman, which would require the FCC to expedite and approve broadband funding application that would serve areas with shorter building seasons, such as areas prone to large snowfall. Anybody who has ever built anything in MI-1 knows that even a small delay before a long winter can be costly.
H .R.1362 - the BOOST Act.
This bill would offer a tax credit up to $400 for certain taxpayers to buy a broadband communications signal booster.
## Veterans' Champion
Veterans’ Champion in Congress
40 years in the Marine Corps and now in his capacity as a leader in the House Veterans Affairs Committee (HVAC), Congressman Bergman has committed his career in Congress to those who served and sacrificed to defend our Nation and our freedoms. He has built his record on tackling the hard issues from toxic exposure and mental health to care in the community and appeals reform.
Representing you on HVAC, Congressman Bergman has assumed leadership roles on the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee and now as the Ranking Member of the Health Subcommittee. In these positions, Congressman Bergman is a fierce watchdog against waste, fraud and abuse – keeping VA’s eye focused on the Veteran as an individual with unique needs.
He uses his position on the Committee to get results for Veterans, including passing new laws to streamline education benefits and save money for servicemembers in boot camp (Public Law 116-315) as well as support and defend the integrity of veteran-owned small businesses (Public Law 116-183). Last Congress, Congressman Bergman spearheaded the national debate on Veterans’ suicide by achieving passage of his bill, the IMPROVE Wellbeing for Veterans Act (Public Law 116-17), a new VA community grant program to connect Veterans in and outside of the VA system with supportive services.
Right now, Congressman Bergman is working on critical new legislation to support Veterans’ Caregivers (H.R.4625 - VA Caregiver Transparency Act),
conduct an independent assessment to audit VA’s health services
(H.R.4626 - VA AIM Act) , and to close various gaps in Veterans care
(H.R.4624 - Guaranteeing Healthcare Access to Personnel Who Served (GHAPS) Act) . Specifically, the GHAPS Act would allow Veterans to self-schedule appointments in the community, improve VA telehealth, protect access to community care, and ensure access to evidence-based care for Veterans with treatment-resistant depression.
Additional actions and achievements in Veterans policy for Congressman Bergman include:
Co-introducing comprehensive legislation to care for and provide benefits to all Veterans with toxic exposure
(H.R.2127 - TEAM Act).
Lead the charge against the Biden VA’s attempts to pay for elective transgender surgeries with tax-payer dollars through letters and amendments.
Co-lead of the bipartisan Congressional Military Transition Assistance Pathway (MTAP) Caucus.
Passed legislation in the House to designate the Gaylord VA facility in the name of Navy Corspman Steve Andrews
## Protecting Michigan's Agriculture
Support for the American Producer
From the farmers, ranchers, and growers to the canners, marketers, and so on, Michigan’s First Congressional District is home to a vibrant agricultural community as well as our Nation’s smartest and hardest working producers. In order to unleash their full potential, Congressman Bergman believes the federal government should always stand as an ally – and never impose burdensome anti-growth regulations on the men and women who feed America.
Congressman Bergman has proudly defended agricultural producers in Congress. He supported the 2018 Farm Bill which reformed and authorized a large slate of nutrition, commodity, research, and other agricultural programs. With the next big Farm Bill on the horizon, he is seeking reelection to make the programs Michigan producers rely on every day more efficient and easier to use.
Overcoming Challenges and Creating Opportunities
Congressman Bergman has been a fierce advocate for pro-agriculture policies, tirelessly having urged swift passage – through speeches, letters, and an Op-Ed in the Detroit News – of the United States - Mexico - Canada Trade Agreement (USMCA). With his help, the
is now the law of the land, casting aside the historical unfair playing field for our farmers to ensure they can compete on an international level. With Michigan exporting billions of dollars worth of goods to Canada and Mexico each year, our state’s agriculture industry – such as our dairy farmers who previously struggled to access Canadian markets – have the groundwork to thrive.
Here in the Nation’s Cherry Capital, Congressman Bergman has led the continued battle against unfair trade practices, having worked with federal agencies and local industry stakeholders. For example, he led the Michigan congressional delegation in the fight against Turkey’s anti-competitive practice of dumping cheap, government subsidized product into our markets. To further support Michigan’s First District tart cherry industry, Congressman Bergman helped secure more than $60 million in surplus product purchases from USDA and advocated for cherry-specific pest research.
Congressman Bergman also helped establish the
Coronavirus Food Assistance Program (CFAP) and achieved inclusion for cherry and apple growers in this farm-saving $16 billion direct payment program.
Additionally, Congressman Bergman is proud to fight for apple, dairy, potato, sugar, and the entire spectrum of products from Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula. Each sector and profession throughout our agricultural industry has unique needs, but one prevalent issue is guest labor. The H-2A program has proven to be costly and difficult to use for many employers, which is why Rep. Bergman is supporting legislation to tame skyrocketing wage rates through cosponsorship of H.R.5887 - Keep Food Local and Affordable Act of 2021.
Congressman Bergman is able to run on a solid pro-producer, pro-agriculture, and pro-growth platform due to the incredible support and education he has received and continues to seek from Michigan’s First agricultural community. There is still much work to be done in securing our domestic supply chains through legislation like H.R. 4996 - the Ocean Shipping Reform Act, responsibly improving our transportation infrastructure, and ensuring more operations have access to high-speed rural broadband.
## Protecting Life - From Birth to Natural Death
The first inalienable right described in the Declaration of Independence is the right to life, and the job of Congress is to protect our rights - not take them away. That includes the lives of those yet born.
Rather than treating pregnancy or children as a problem, we should work together to create a society that welcomes them into our communities with loving and open arms. We must remember that every person is a unique child of God, full of potential. As a member of Congress, Congressman Bergman has worked to protect the unborn and move the pro-life message forward.
Congressman Bergman is a Member of the Congressional Pro Life Caucus, and has cosponsored the
No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion Act (H.R. 18) . This legislation prohibits the use of federal funds for abortions or for health coverage that includes abortions.
Since coming to Congress, Congressman Bergman has also supported the
Pain Capable Unborn Child Protection Act (H.R.1080) which bans abortions after the 20 th week of pregnancy. This legislation is widely supported throughout the First District and across the country.
Congressman Bergman has supported other important pro-life legislation, such as:
- The Born Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act: this legislation would protect a child born alive after surviving an abortion and require healthcare practitioners present to exercise the same care to preserve the life and health of the child as a non-aborted child who was premature.
- The Conscious Protection Act:
this legislation would prohibit the federal government and state and local governments that receive federal financial assistance for health-related activities penalizing or discriminating against a health care provider based on the provider's refusal to be involved in, or provide coverage for, abortion.
- H.R. 243, the Title X Abortion Provider Prohibition Act of 2021.
- H.R. 28, the Protecting Life in Crisis Act of 2021.
- H.R. 541, the Defund Planned Parenthood Act of 2021.
## National Security
As someone who was personally involved in the fight to defend our country from terrorism, Congressman Bergman knows what the military needs to defeat our enemies. He has seen the horrors of war and understands that, under the Constitution, the most important vote a member of Congress can make is whether or not to send our troops into battle.
He is fully committed to only support the use of troops when it is absolutely necessary. When the threat requires the deployment of our military, Congressman Bergman will ensure that our troops are trained and equipped to win decisively and return home to their families.
## Education
Thomas Jefferson once said, “An educated citizenry is a vital requisite for our survival as a free people.” He was right! The government monopoly on education for a large portion of Americans is a tragedy and should be viewed as the modern civil rights issue of our time. We need to offer education reform that supports more choice in education, from public schooling to home schooling. Everyone in the United States deserves a great education.
## Immigration
Border security is National Security.
We are a welcoming Nation, but we are a Nation of rule of law. While we must continue being generous, we should never allow it for people who intend to do us harm or who violate our immigration laws.
Congressman Bergman has supported important policies to secure our border and put our Nation first.
He cosponsored legislation to address the current crisis and some of its root causes, such as H.R.88 - the BUILD WALL Act of 2021 , which would use assets seized from Mexican cartels to build further border security infrastructure.
H.R. 894 – No Tax Breaks for Sanctuary Cities Act to revoke the tax exemption for bonds issued by jurisdictions which refuse to comply with immigration enforcement.
Congressman Bergman cosponsored H.R.1901 – Fix Immigration Loopholes Act , which would both disincentivize illegal immigration by increasing the integrity of our Nation’s asylum process and also protect children from becoming human trafficking victims by ensuring they are processed efficiently to be quickly and safely returned home and only released to a parent or legal guardian.
In 2019, Rep. Bergman supported an additional $1.9 billion for border wall and security funding.
## Protecting Our Natural Resources
We live where we do for a reason. This land that we call home is the most beautiful place in all of our nation, and we cannot allow our Natural Resources to be damaged. That is why I have successfully led the fight to ensure that all Great Lakes funding remain in place since taking office. I have fought to ensure a plan is in place to stop Asian carp from entering our Great lakes, and have introduced legislation to effectively control the Cormorants that are devastating our fish population. Through the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, I helped secure the largest investment in the Great Lakes in over two decades — ensuring we protect our most important resource for generations to come.
## Opioid Epidemic
In 2019 alone, more than 50,000 lives were lost to opioids. It stuns me when I realize that something intended to help people has also done so much harm to our nation. This is not a simple problem and there are no simple solutions, but Congress must take a comprehensive approach to target every factor in this issue. I will continue to engage with various groups in our communities so I can effectively address the issues specific to Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula.

## Rural Broadband Connectivity, Now!
One of the largest broadband investments in Michigan's First District came through the FCC's Rural Digital Opportunity Fund. The program committed approximately
$205.5 million to expand broadband to an estimated 87,503 homes and businesses across MI-01.
Bergman has also supported key federal programs bringing broadband infrastructure to rural communities, including the
USDA ReConnect Program and Distance Learning and Telemedicine Grants, while working with local providers and communities seeking federal support.
Congressman Bergman regularly works directly with broadband providers and the Federal Communications Commission to resolve delays, address grant and payment issues, and help move federal funding to projects serving Northern Michigan communities.
In 2020, as COVID-19 dramatically increased the need for reliable internet access, Bergman supported billions in emergency broadband funding for telehealth, broadband infrastructure, mapping, and keeping families connected.
## Cutting Red Tape:
Bergman has also introduced legislation specifically designed around the challenges of building broadband in Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula.
Rural Broadband Window of Opportunity Act , reintroduced in 2025, would require the FCC to prioritize certain broadband applications in areas with shorter construction seasons.
Anyone who has built anything in Northern Michigan knows why that matters - a bureaucratic delay before winter can mean losing an entire year of construction.
Bergman has also introduced the
Big Tech Accountability for Broadband Act , which would require major technology companies that benefit from expanded connectivity to contribute to the Universal Service Fund rather than continuing to place the burden primarily on telecommunications customers.
From supporting broadband infrastructure to cutting federal red tape, Congressman Jack Bergman will continue working to connect rural America and ensure Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula aren't left behind.
## Veterans' Champion
After 40 years in the United States Marine Corps, Rep. Jack Bergman has continued his commitment to those who served our Nation through his work on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
Bergman has served on the Veterans' Affairs Committee since his first term in Congress and currently serves on both the Health and Oversight and Investigations Subcommittees. He has focused his work on improving Veterans' health care, expanding access to innovative treatments, strengthening community care, preventing Veteran suicide, protecting earned benefits, and holding the Department of Veterans Affairs accountable.
## Delivering Results
Bergman has helped turn bipartisan Veterans priorities into law.
IMPROVE Well-Being for Veterans Act established a new VA community grant program designed to connect at-risk Veterans - including those outside the traditional VA system - with local organizations and suicide-prevention services. He also helped advance major reforms expanding Veterans' access to home and community-based care through the
Elizabeth Dole 21st Century Veterans Healthcare and Benefits Improvement Act .
That law also included a pilot provision based on Bergman's
Gerald's Law , named for Dickinson County Veteran Gerald "Jerry" Elliott. The provision addresses a gap that denied burial benefits to certain terminally ill Veterans who left a VA facility to receive VA-furnished hospice care at home. In 2026, Bergman reintroduced Gerald's Law to make that protection permanent.
## Expanding and Improving Veterans' Health Care
Bergman continues to lead bipartisan efforts aimed at improving the quality of care Veterans receive, including:
- BEACON Act - Introduced in 2026 to expand access to innovative, evidence-based, non-pharmacological treatments for Veterans living with traumatic brain injuries.
- Veterans STAND Act - Bipartisan legislation to ensure Veterans with spinal cord injuries and disorders receive comprehensive annual evaluations and are considered for advanced assistive technologies, including powered exoskeletons and other treatments that can improve mobility and independence.
- NOPAIN for Veterans Act - Bipartisan legislation to expand Veterans' access to non-opioid pain management options covered by Medicare, providing additional alternatives to addictive opioid medications.
- RELIEVE Act - Bipartisan legislation aimed at closing a gap in VA community care and protecting Veterans' coverage for emergency medical treatment.
- CHOICE for Veterans Act - Legislation advanced by the House Veterans' Affairs Committee to crack down on unaccredited claims agents who exploit Veterans while establishing stronger safeguards for Veterans seeking assistance with disability claims.
## Fighting Veteran Suicide and Expanding Mental Health Care
Veteran suicide prevention has remained a central focus of Bergman's work. In 2026, Bergman introduced the bipartisan
Improving Mental Health Support for Servicemembers and Veterans Act , which would require a formal review of federal mental health programs for Veterans and transitioning servicemembers to identify gaps, duplication, and barriers to care.
He also led a bipartisan group of
29 Members of Congress in seeking full funding for VA suicide prevention and treatment programs in the FY27 appropriations process.
Bergman has additionally pushed federal agencies to expand Veterans' access to promising new treatments for mental health conditions and traumatic brain injuries.
## Protecting Veterans and Their Families
Bergman's work extends beyond health care. His
GRACE for Military Survivors Act , introduced in 2026, would give surviving military family members more time and flexibility to make important financial decisions regarding survivor benefits following the loss of a servicemember.
Bergman has also fought to strengthen VA financial accountability, protect Veterans from fraud and predatory actors, and ensure taxpayer dollars intended for Veterans actually reach the men and women who earned those benefits.
From improving care for Veterans with traumatic brain injuries and spinal cord injuries to preventing suicide, protecting survivor benefits, expanding treatment options, and holding the VA accountable, Rep. Jack Bergman has made serving those who served a cornerstone of his work in Congress.
## Supporting Michigan's Agriculture
Agriculture is essential to the economy and way of life of Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula. Congressman Bergman has worked to support Michigan producers, protect family farms, expand markets, and fight unfair foreign competition.
## Delivering for Michigan Agriculture
In 2026, Congressman Bergman voted to pass the Farm, Food, and National Security Act, strengthening the farm safety net, specialty crop programs, crop insurance, agricultural trade promotion, and voluntary conservation programs.
Representing the Cherry Capital of the World, Congressman Bergman has made Michigan's cherry industry a priority. He helped secure more than $60 million in USDA purchases of surplus tart cherries, fought unfair trade practices involving subsidized Turkish cherry products, and pushed for additional assistance and research for Michigan growers.
## Protecting Family Farms
Congressman Bergman helped lead 74 Members of Congress in introducing the bipartisan Family Farm and Small Business Exemption Act, protecting family farms and small businesses from being unfairly counted against students seeking financial aid.
## Expanding Markets
Congressman Bergman strongly advocated for the USMCA, supported the Ocean Shipping Reform Act, and helped secure pandemic-era assistance for Michigan cherry and apple growers.
In 2026, he supported nationwide, year-round E15 ethanol sales to expand domestic demand for American-grown corn. He has also pushed USDA to increase purchases of American-grown specialty crops for schools, food banks, nutrition programs, and the Department of Defense.
## Protecting American Agriculture
Congressman Bergman has supported legislation to prevent entities connected to the Chinese government from purchasing American agricultural land and has fought to return management of the gray wolf to state wildlife professionals.
From cherries and apples to dairy, potatoes, maple syrup, forestry, and specialty crops, Congressman Bergman will continue fighting for Michigan producers, family farms, and the rural communities that feed America.
## Protecting Life
The first inalienable right recognized in the Declaration of Independence is the right to life. Congressman Bergman believes Congress has a responsibility to protect that right, including for the unborn, while supporting a culture that welcomes children and strengthens families.
Throughout his time in Congress, Congressman Bergman has consistently supported pro-life policies, including efforts to:
- Prevent taxpayer funding of abortion
and protect longstanding federal pro-life provisions. Congressman Bergman has supported legislation to prohibit federal funding for abortion and has fought to preserve the Hyde Amendment.
- Protect infants born alive following an attempted abortion.
In 2025, Congressman Bergman voted for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act, requiring appropriate medical care for children born alive following an attempted abortion.
- Protect conscience rights
for health care professionals who object to participating in abortion procedures.
- Support pro-life protections for families and taxpayers
through legislation and federal funding policy.
Congressman Bergman will continue working to protect life, defend conscience rights, and support policies that strengthen mothers, children, and families.
## Peace Through Strength
After 40 years in the United States Marine Corps, including service as a helicopter pilot in Vietnam and ultimately as a Lieutenant General and Commander of Marine Forces Reserve and Marine Forces North, Congressman Jack Bergman understands firsthand the responsibility that comes with sending America's sons and daughters into harm's way.
Congressman Bergman believes America's military must be strong enough to deter our adversaries and ready to decisively defeat any threat to our Nation. When our troops are called upon, they must have the training, equipment, leadership, and support necessary to accomplish their mission and return home safely.
## Leading on Military Readiness
Congressman Bergman serves on the House Armed Services Committee and was selected in 2025 to serve as
Chairman of the Subcommittee on Readiness , putting him in a key leadership position overseeing the readiness of America's Armed Forces.
As Chairman, Congressman Bergman has focused on rebuilding military readiness, improving maintenance of America's aircraft, ships, vehicles, and equipment, strengthening military infrastructure, cutting waste and bureaucracy, and ensuring our warfighters are prepared for the threats of today and tomorrow. In 2026, Congressman Bergman continued pressing military leaders on declining readiness rates and the need to properly maintain and sustain the equipment America already owns.
## Strengthening America's Military
Congressman Bergman has helped shape and pass annual National Defense Authorization Acts to strengthen America's military and support the men and women who serve.
FY26 National Defense Authorization Act included major priorities Congressman Bergman championed as Readiness Chairman, including:
3.8% pay raise for servicemembers and extending important bonuses and special pays.
- Modernizing America's military capabilities and strengthening the defense industrial base.
- Reforming defense acquisition to get needed technology and equipment into the hands of warfighters faster.
- Strengthening America's missile defense, nuclear deterrent, aircraft, submarine, and autonomous-system capabilities.
- Investing in military housing and quality of life for servicemembers and their families.
- Requiring greater accountability and transparency for PFAS cleanup at military installations, including
Camp Grayling and the former Wurtsmith Air Force Base .
Congressman Bergman has continued that work through the
FY27 NDAA , supporting investments in military readiness, servicemember pay, education, childcare, and America's national defense.
## Supporting Michigan's Military Mission
Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula play an important role in America's national defense.
Congressman Bergman has consistently fought for
Camp Grayling and Northern Strike , one of the Department of Defense's largest reserve-component exercises, bringing together thousands of servicemembers and partner forces for advanced joint training in Northern Michigan.
He has also worked to address PFAS contamination associated with military installations. In 2025, Congressman Bergman introduced the bipartisan
Military PFAS Transparency Act , requiring greater transparency and accountability from the Department of Defense regarding cleanup efforts at contaminated military sites.
Key provisions of that effort were incorporated into the FY26 NDAA, including requirements for cleanup plans, risk assessments, and safeguards affecting communities around Camp Grayling, Wurtsmith, and military installations nationwide.
## Confronting America's Adversaries
Congressman Bergman has pushed to ensure the United States has the capabilities necessary to deter threats from China, Russia, Iran, terrorist organizations, and other adversaries.
Chairman of the House Armed Services Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittee during the 118th Congress , Congressman Bergman oversaw critical national intelligence, counterterrorism, and special operations issues.
He also helped advance the FY25 NDAA, which strengthened America's ability to counter the Chinese Communist Party, enhanced intelligence and counterintelligence capabilities, strengthened biodefense preparedness, and supported Taiwan's ability to defend itself.
## Supporting the National Guard and Reserve
Having commanded Marine Forces Reserve, Congressman Bergman understands the unique role America's Reserve Component plays in our national defense.
In 2026, Congressman Bergman helped lead the bipartisan
Duty Status Reform Act , legislation designed to simplify the nearly 30 different duty statuses currently affecting National Guard and Reserve servicemembers.
The legislation would streamline those classifications, improve consistency in pay and benefits, reduce administrative confusion, and make it easier for commanders to mobilize forces when America needs them.
## Putting Warfighters First
Congressman Bergman's approach to national security is rooted in a simple principle:
peace through strength.
That means maintaining the force America already has, investing in the capabilities needed to deter our adversaries, supporting our servicemembers and their families, cutting waste and bureaucracy at the Pentagon, and ensuring America's military remains the most capable and lethal fighting force in the world.
Congressman Jack Bergman will continue using his experience as a Marine and his leadership on the House Armed Services Committee to ensure America's warfighters are trained, equipped, and ready whenever our Nation calls.
## Education
Congressman Bergman believes every child deserves a quality education and that parents - not Washington bureaucrats - should have the strongest voice in deciding what's best for their children.
That means supporting educational freedom, whether families choose public, private, charter, career and technical education, or homeschooling.
Congressman Bergman has backed that commitment with action. He reintroduced the
School Resource Officer Funding Protection Act to protect school safety funding and helped lead the bipartisan
Family Farm and Small Business Exemption Act to ensure family farms and small businesses aren't unfairly counted against students seeking financial aid.
He has also supported efforts to increase transparency and prevent foreign adversaries like the Chinese Communist Party from influencing American schools.
Congressman Bergman will continue fighting for
parental rights, school choice, safe schools, and greater opportunities for every student to succeed.
## Border Security is National Security
America is a welcoming Nation, but we are also a Nation of laws. Congressman Bergman believes securing our borders is essential to protecting our communities, stopping the flow of deadly drugs, combating human trafficking, and defending our national security.
Congressman Bergman has consistently supported stronger border enforcement and immigration laws. He supported the
Secure the Border Act , comprehensive legislation to strengthen border security, reform the asylum process, increase Border Patrol resources, and address loopholes in our immigration system.
In 2025, Congressman Bergman supported the
Laken Riley Act, which expanded federal detention requirements for certain illegal immigrants charged with or convicted of specified crimes. The legislation was signed into law in January 2025.
Congressman Bergman also introduced the
VOICE Restoration Act to restore the Victims of Immigration Crime Engagement Office and provide resources and support to victims and families affected by crimes committed by illegal immigrants.
He also supported the
One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which provided major new investments in border security and immigration enforcement, including resources for border infrastructure, personnel, detention capacity, and efforts to stop fentanyl trafficking.
Congressman Bergman has also supported legislation to strengthen border technology, combat illegal entry, and ensure federal resources are focused on enforcing our Nation's immigration laws.
Congressman Bergman will continue fighting to secure America's borders, enforce our laws, stop the flow of fentanyl, and protect American communities.
## Protecting Our Great Lakes & Natural Resources
We live here for a reason. Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula are home to some of the most beautiful land, water, forests, and wildlife anywhere in America. Congressman Bergman believes we have a responsibility to protect these resources while ensuring they remain accessible to the people who live, work, hunt, fish, and recreate here.
Congressman Bergman has consistently fought to protect and strengthen the
Great Lakes Restoration Initiative (GLRI) and helped introduce bipartisan legislation to extend the program through 2031 and increase authorized funding to
$500 million annually .
He has also been a leading voice in the fight to stop invasive carp from reaching the Great Lakes. In 2025, Congressman Bergman pushed to restart the
Brandon Road Interbasin Project , a critical barrier designed to prevent invasive carp from entering Lake Michigan, and continued pressing for federal action to move the project forward.
Congressman Bergman has also worked to:
- Protect Great Lakes fisheries from invasive species, including
sea lamprey and cormorants .
- Return management of the
gray wolf to state wildlife professionals.
- Protect access to
hunting, fishing, and recreational shooting on federal lands.
- Strengthen forest health and reforestation through the bipartisan
RNGR Support Act , including support for the J.W. Toumey Nursery in Michigan's First District.
- Secure assistance for
farmers and forest landowners recovering from the historic 2025 Northern Michigan ice storm.
From protecting the Great Lakes and our fisheries to maintaining healthy forests and defending access to Michigan's outdoors, Congressman Bergman will continue working to preserve our natural resources for generations to come.
